item.title: Luminescent materials based on aromatic bisimides—part 1: the smaller pyromellitic and naphthalene derivatives
item.description:
Authors: Swadhin Garain, Menyhárt B. Sárosi, Subi J. George, Frank Würthner

This review describes the advancements in the development and application of small aromatic bisimides, with a particular focus on their fluorescence, thermally activated delayed fluorescence, phosphorescence, and circularly polarised luminescence.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00323k

item.title: Transition metal-based nanocatalysts for bidirectional immunomodulation: from catalytic anti-inflammation to catalytic immunotherapy
item.description:
Authors: Bowen Yang, Jianlin Shi

This tutorial review elucidates the chemical basis of nanocatalytic bidirectional immunomodulation, highlighting how transition metal-based nanocatalysts suppress hyperactive immunity and activate suppressed immunity for disease treatments.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs01262k

item.title: Porous materials for sulfur dioxide capture from flue gas
item.description:
Authors: Yiting Guo, Ziyi Luo, Ru Xu, Lin Li, Xuan Zhang, Yabing He, Xian-He Bu, Banglin Chen

This review summarizes recent advances in porous materials for SO 2 capture, compares their adsorption mechanisms and structure–performance relationships, and highlights challenges and prospects for flue gas desulfurization.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs01116k

item.title: What if we were to design transport in aqueous electrolytes using learnings from lithium battery research?
item.description:
Authors: Alexa Hanlon, Charles Schreiber, Trevor Sando, Edward Mather, Bree Mitchell, Aashutosh Mistry

Aqueous battery electrolyte design heuristics for improved transport are identified herein, and considerably differ from the lithium electrolyte designs.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00073h

item.title: Aggregation-induced radical
item.description:
Authors: Siqin Huang, Yanfei Shi, Yuan Li

Differing from the aromaticity recovery-stabilized radicals explored since 1907 and AIE, we elaborate the mechanism, experimental and theoretical validation, material design, potential application and future directions of the AIR concept with ACQ.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00342g

item.title: Luminescent radicals – synthesis, photophysics and applications
item.description:
Authors: Bartosz Godlewski, Olena Vakuliuk, Wojciech D. Petrykowski, Beata Koszarna, Krzysztof Górski, Mariusz Tasior, Yevgen M. Poronik, Krzysztof J. Kochanowski, Łukasz W. Ciszewski, Anna M. Grabarz, Denis Jacquemin, Daniel T. Gryko

Room temperature luminescent radicals stormed the literature in the last decade. Structure-properties relationship as well as synthetic and computational aspects are reviewed. Overview of applications is presented.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00975a

item.title: Radical addition approaches for 2m/2π-intermolecular reactions of alkenes and alkynes
item.description:
Authors: Nikita S. Shlapakov, Andrey D. Kobelev, Valentine P. Ananikov

This review organizes radical intermolecular reactions of two π-components through the 2m/2π-synthon framework, highlighting the main strategies used to sort alkene and alkyne partners.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00676k

item.title: Contemporary synthetic tools for the total synthesis of natural products
item.description:
Authors: Finlay Blackwell, Ben Harper, Himani Mistry, Ivan Zlatkov, Peilin Tian, Edward A. Anderson

This Tutorial Review discusses uses of modern synthetic tools in the total synthesis of natural products over the last five years, including photocatalysis, electrochemistry, biocatalysis, skeletal editing, flow chemistry and mechanochemistry.

DOI: 10.1039/d5cs01517k

item.title: Antifreeze proteins in action: structural determinants, hydration dynamics, and ice-binding mechanisms
item.description:
Authors: Prasun Pal, Sandipan Chakraborty, Biman Jana

Anchored by classical nucleation theory, this review connects the structural diversity of antifreeze and ice-nucleating proteins to their ice-binding mechanisms and extends to cryopreservation, anti-icing, and AI-driven mimetic design.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs01160h

item.title: Silanols in zeolite catalysis: from defects to designable functionality
item.description:
Authors: Ye Ding, Fuyuan Hao, Jiachun Su, Xutong Meng, Mei-Yan Wang, Ji Qi, Shouying Huang, Xinbin Ma

Zeolite silanols were long treated mainly as structural defects, but recent catalytic studies show that specific silanol populations can also function as catalytically relevant sites or local environments.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00169f

item.title: In-field crop disease surveillance: from phenotypes to molecules
item.description:
Authors: Xuhan Xia, Ting Zhang, Qiuyu Luo, Honghong Wu, Qingshan Wei, Ruijie Deng

This review outlines crop pathogen biomarkers and in-field molecular detection advances, evaluates in-field tool readiness, and details their applications in early disease detection, field pathogen survey, pesticide guidance, and mechanism research.

DOI: 10.1039/d5cs01551k

item.title: Monolayer molecular crystals: controlled-growth technologies, structure–property relationships, and device applications
item.description:
Authors: Yuanyuan Zhang, Daowei He, Tao Zhang, Guocai Liu, Chengliang Wang, Lang Jiang

This review establishes a mechanism-driven framework for monolayer molecular crystals (MMCs), integrating controlled growth, structure–property relationships, and device applications. It outlines pathways toward scalable molecular electronics.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs01235c

item.title: Electrochemical conversion of low-concentration carbon dioxide to multicarbon products: advances, challenges, and perspectives
item.description:
Authors: Xuanzhao Lu, Chen Qin, Jingyao Xia, Baozhen Yuan, Tangrui Li, Chen Zhou, Yujing Jiang, Ao Xia, Bing Song, Richen Lin, Wenlei Zhu

This review highlights advances in electrochemical conversion of low-concentration CO 2 to multicarbon products, covering dilute and impurity-containing CO 2 , capture-solution electrolysis, bioelectrocatalysis, and techno-economic analysis.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00916f

item.title: Hydrogen borrowing with heterogeneous catalysis
item.description:
Authors: Karel Weemaes, Robby Vroemans, Guangxin Xue, Henrik Junge, Sergey Sergeyev, Matthias Beller, Bert U. W. Maes

Hydrogen borrowing (HB) enables sustainable C–N, C–C, and C–S bond formation using alcohols as alkylating agents. Heterogeneous HB catalysts offer improved recyclability and scalability (continuous production).

DOI: 10.1039/d3cs00314k
